subject: English
passage: Today photographer Ansel Adams is primarily known for his iconic black-and-white landscape photographs of Yosemite and the American West. However, by focusing only on his most famous images, viewers miss the breadth of Adams's artistic vision. For example, his intimate portraits and his experimental color work from the 1940s demonstrate his ability to capture both human emotion and innovative techniques. These overlooked photographs merit the same recognition as his celebrated wilderness scenes.
prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To compare the artistic merits of black-and-white versus color photography
choices.B: To encourage photography enthusiasts to study works by various artists
choices.C: To argue that Adams's lesser-known photographs deserve greater appreciation
choices.D: To explain how Adams developed his distinctive photographic style

explanation:
Choice C is the best answer because it best states the main purpose of the text, which is to make a case for the importance of Ansel Adams's less famous works. The text begins by introducing Adams's most popular photographs and then goes on to assert that gaining a full understanding of Adams's artistic vision requires consideration of his lesser-known pieces as well. The text concludes by characterizing the overlooked works as photographs that "merit the same recognition" as his celebrated images. These details indicate that the text's main purpose is to argue that Adams's lesser-known photographs deserve greater appreciation.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect. Although the text mentions both black-and-white landscapes and color work that Adams created, it does not compare the two photographic techniques in general. Instead, the text argues that Adams's lesser-known works, including his color photographs, deserve as much attention as his more famous black-and-white images receive.
